subject: BrightMaps: unexpected mid-month embeddings usage spike — reconciliation & credit
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightmaps.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden embed usage spike on Jun 14 — please advise

Hi Neha,

We noticed a large jump in our embeddings usage on Jun 14 that pushed us ~210% over our usual daily volume and generated an unexpected mid-cycle overage. Our ingestion job did run that day but we don't have any duplicate runs in our logs. I attached our export from our internal job (brightmaps_usage_export_2027-06-14_to_2027-06-15.csv).

Can you confirm how Redwood meters embedding requests (per-call vs per-vector), and whether there's any known issue that might double-count batching windows? We need the breakdown to reconcile with accounting.

Also looping in procurement (procurement@brightmaps.com) because they'll likely ask for a credit if this is on you.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Data Engineering
BrightMaps

Attachments: brightmaps_usage_export_2027-06-14_to_2027-06-15.csv (csv)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightmaps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden embed usage spike on Jun 14 — please advise

Thanks for the heads-up, Lena — I’m looking into this. Quick answers up front:

- Embeddings are billed per vector generated; we also include a small per-request overhead for metadata.
- We have a continuous batching layer; in rare edge cases a client-side retry + batching boundary can result in duplicate vectors being persisted to the aggregation window.

Next steps from our side:
1) I’ve pulled the server-side usage snapshot for your account for 2027-06-14 and attached a matching export.
2) I’ve asked Billing (cc: Ben) to provisionally review the overage and propose a remedial credit if the spike is on us.
3) Please confirm whether the attached CSV represents the full set of client-side requests around 14:00–18:00 PDT on Jun 14 — if you have request IDs we can correlate them to our logs.

I’ve attached redwood_usage_snapshot_2027-06-14.csv with token/vector counts per hour. If you can send the request IDs or the job run id we’ll do a line-by-line correlation.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_usage_snapshot_2027-06-14.csv (csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden embed usage spike on Jun 14 — please advise

On Wed, Jun 15, 2027 at 11:02 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> I’ve attached redwood_usage_snapshot_2027-06-14.csv with token/vector counts per hour.

Thanks for pulling the snapshot. I reviewed the server export and compared to the CSV BrightMaps provided. Two notable items:

- There is a cluster of ~37k vectors during 14:12–14:18 PDT that do not match any request IDs in BrightMaps’ CSV; bucket-level correlation suggests those were replays from a short-lived retry loop on our ingress layer.
- Our logs show the ingress received duplicated POSTs with identical payload digests from a single IP for three minutes; that pattern typically indicates a client-side retry mechanism interacting with an upstream timeout.

Recommendation:
- We should offer a one-time usage credit that covers the duplicated vectors for Jun 14 (we estimate 37,200 vectors * unit price = $X — we’ll compute exact amount once finance confirms rate card).
- Ask the customer to confirm whether they want throttles or idempotency keys enabled for that specific job moving forward; we can provide an idempotent API header guide.

On tax/VAT: BrightMaps is US-registered per HubSpot (BRM-1284). No EU VAT reverse-charge applies. If procurement needs a consolidated credit memo we’ll issue it against invoice INV-20270601 after they confirm the contact and PO.

I’ll draft the credit note and loop in Finance for the actual dollar amount. Vanessa — please advise the usual timeline for issuing one-off credits and whether we need a signed credit confirmation from the customer.

- Ben
Senior Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightmaps.com>, procurement@brightmaps.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden embed usage spike on Jun 14 — please advise

Hi Lena / BrightMaps procurement,

Thanks for confirming the job export. We reconciled your CSV with our server-side export and found ~37.2k vectors that appear to be duplicated on Redwood’s ingress due to a brief retry window. Ben has proposed a one-time credit; Finance has approved a provisional credit and we prepared a draft credit note (attached: proposed_credit_note_BRM-20270621.pdf).

Action items:
- Please confirm the PO/Invoice to apply the credit against (we suggest INV-20270601).
- Confirm whether you want us to enable idempotency-key guidance for the job (we can configure an SDK snippet and a short runbook).
- If you need a signed confirmation before Finance applies the credit, reply with an approval sentence (e.g., “BrightMaps approves the credit of $YYY to INV-20270601”).

We’ll finalize and post the credit within 3 business days after we receive your approval and the PO reference. No VAT adjustments are necessary for this US customer.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll also provide the idempotency/ingress guidance to avoid recurrence.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_credit_note_BRM-20270621.pdf (pdf)
